series.source: Statistics Sweden (SCB), average monthly salary after sector, all sectors, total gender.
series.unit: SEK/month; annual comparator calculated as monthly × 12
series.definition: SCB average monthly salary across all sectors, both sexes (total gender), for each year 1992–2025. Salary is not disposable income or actual annual earnings.
series.transformation: Annual comparator is monthly average multiplied by 12; nominal values. Monthly source values retained in the separate salary file.

series.source: Sveriges Riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden, Volume I, Svante Prado workbook, Tables I.A10.1 and I.A10.2.
series.definition: Hourly earnings by manufacturing industry category and sex, plus a separately identified source-provided weighted average. Source table categories are represented in Swedish in the CSV.
series.coverage: Sweden; manufacturing workers. Coverage varies by industry and sex. Male categories are observed from 1860 or later depending on category; female coverage starts between 1865 and 1952 by category. Male weighted average 1871–2013; female weighted average 1921–2013.
series.transformation: Transcribed source observations without annualization or interpolation. Missing cells are omitted. This sectoral hourly series is not directly equivalent to all-sector monthly salary; overlap does not imply equivalent population or method.

series.source: Energimyndigheten, Energiläget i siffror 2026, Table 5.5, source note: SCB and Drivkraft Sverige; nominal values derived with SCB annual-average CPI.
series.definition: Annual average Swedish pump price for gasoline 95 octane (MK1/MK2), including taxes and VAT, as reported in Energimyndigheten table 5.5 in 2024 price level and converted back to nominal SEK. National annual series; product specification and fuel blend may vary over time.
series.coverage: Sweden, national annual average, 1980–2025. Separate pre-war reported price ranges are preserved in gasoline_historical_price_ranges.csv; they are tax-exclusive and not directly comparable with this series.
series.transformation: Calculated as source price in 2024 SEK × SCB annual-average CPI for observation year ÷ SCB annual-average CPI for 2024; rounded to öre. No interpolation.

series.source: Swedish Parliament, Första kammarens andra tillfälliga utskotts utlåtande nr 14 (1945), plus the 1948 official SOU and 1954 Government proposition for individual O-zone price observations.
series.definition: The 1925–1939 entries are the source's minimum and maximum retail-price quotations with gasoline tax excluded. The 1948 O-zone price is reported as 66 öre/liter with taxes; the 1953 O-zone figure is an October price calculation of 59 öre/liter with taxes. None of these points is a national annual mean or a consistent fuel specification.
series.coverage: Sweden, reported quotation ranges 1925–1939 plus individual O-zone observations in 1948 and 1953. There are no entries for 1940–1947, 1949–1952, or 1954–1979. The national annual pump-price series begins in 1980.
series.transformation: Transcribed min/max source values as öre per litre; where the source gives a point price, min equals max and the observation type identifies it. No averaging, tax adjustment, conversion to a single series, or interpolation.

series.source: Swedish Parliament and Government: historical radio licence values and radio/TV fee milestones from 1925 onward; SOU 2005:2 table of annual TV fees for 1991–2005; parliamentary statutory changes and reports for 2006–2018; parliamentary and Swedish Tax Agency values for the public service fee 2019–2025.
series.unit: SEK per year in force at 31 December; household (1991–2018), maximum per person (2019–2025)
series.definition: Annual radio and TV fee payable by one household with a TV receiver through 2018. From 2019, maximum individual public service fee, levied through income tax at 1 percent of taxable earned income up to a yearly cap. The fee type and liable unit changed on 2019-01-01.
series.coverage: Sweden, annual rates where the sources document a rate or a period at a fixed rate: radio licence from 1925; selected dated radio/TV fee rates through 1990; continuous annual rate series 1991–2025. Remaining gap in this dataset: 1967–1968. Newly documented coverage fills 1972–1987. Salary comparison is available for 1992–2025; historical hourly manufacturing wages are a separate population and unit. The series starts in 1925, when the public broadcast receiver licence began; earlier radio transmitter permits are a different fee and are not represented.
series.transformation: Records rate in force on 31 December where a dated transition is documented, not the amount actually paid during that calendar year. Annual values 1926–1950 and 1951–1955 use source statements that the rate was unchanged over those spans. 1956–1958 includes explicitly marked limited TV rollout/national coverage and radio-plus-TV fee; 1969 onward represents the household receiver fee, with color-TV supplement included where the source gives it. The 1972–1976 combined TV/radio receiver amount is 220 SEK general fee plus 100 SEK colour-TV surcharge; from 1977–1980 it is 280 + 120 SEK; 1981–1982 it is 508 + 160 SEK; 1983–1984 it is 548 + 160 SEK; 1985 is 648 + 160 SEK; and 1986–1987 is 708 + 160 SEK. These yearly values follow the effective dates and unchanged periods documented in parliamentary/government materials. 1991–2018 is the household TV rate; 2019–2025 is the statutory individual maximum. Relative share is amount ÷ SCB average annual gross salary × 100 for En vuxen. Familj assumes two adults each earning SCB average: household rates counted once; individual maximum fees counted twice; denominator doubled. Trends are only calculated for adjacent years in the same documented regime; missing years remain gaps. No values are interpolated.

series.source: Energimyndigheten, Energiläget i siffror 2026, Table 5.5; source note in workbook: SCB and Drivkraft Sverige.
series.definition: Annual average pump price, gasoline 95 octane (MK1/MK2), including taxes and VAT, in 2024 price level.
series.transformation: Source values copied as published; this source-level file is retained separately from the derived nominal price file.

series.source: Statistics Sweden (SCB), Consumer Price Index (CPI), fixed index rebased to 2020=100, monthly observations aggregated to calendar-year arithmetic average.
series.definition: Annual arithmetic average of the 12 monthly fixed CPI index values. Rebased values preserve the year-to-year price-level ratio used for deflation/reflation.
series.transformation: Arithmetic mean of monthly values; CPI is used only to convert the gasoline series between 2024 prices and nominal annual SEK.

series.source: FZ.se's 2017 summary of Swedish new console prices, based on Cuponation's compilation from historical Swedish articles and forums including FZ, Aftonbladet and Sweclockers.
series.unit: nominal SEK per console at Swedish launch
series.definition: Reported Swedish new retail price at launch for the original Nintendo console model; these are discrete product launch observations, not calendar-year average retail prices.
series.coverage: Sweden; six Nintendo consoles with prices reported for 1992, 1997, 2002, 2006, 2012 and 2017. NES is omitted: FZ reports 1987, while other sources document Swedish retail availability from 1 September 1986, and no contemporaneous price source was verified. This is a secondary compilation, not a primary price list.
series.transformation: Prices transcribed from the nominal-price column. Wage share is launch price divided by SCB average monthly salary for the same year × 12 × 100; family share uses twice that annual wage. No inflation adjustment. No trend arrow is calculated between different hardware models.

series.source: Bergsala/Nintendo Sweden annual promotional brochures, preserved as scans by RL Vision; brochure years 1988–1993. The scans document Swedish game catalogues but the inspected catalogue pages do not show a verifiable price series.
series.definition: Intended annual measure is the arithmetic mean of documented Swedish new-retail prices for Nintendo games in a dated source sample. Each published year must state the sample size and sampling basis; it must not be presented as a market-wide mean unless the source coverage supports that claim.
series.coverage: NES entered Swedish retail 1 September 1986. Brochure scans inspected cover 1988–1993, but do not provide verifiable price observations. The CSV therefore intentionally contains headers only; no annual average game-price value is currently verified.
series.transformation: No value until a reproducible annual sample of comparable Swedish new-game prices is transcribed. Average only observations within a documented source/sample definition; keep years with no evidence blank. Exclude second-hand prices and do not interpolate.
